beginner: Standard broccoli is the go-to: a mild, fresh microgreen from small seeds you scatter dry (no soaking), ready in about 8 to 12 days. seasoned: For a steady supply, stagger sowings: start a fresh broccoli tray every 3 to 5 days rather than one big tray at once. Indoors there is no season, so the cadence is limited only by your tray count and counter space.

beginner: Broccoli microgreens are baby broccoli plants that you harvest very young, about 8 to 12 days after planting, when they are just a couple of inches tall. You grow them indoors all year on a shallow tray of seed-starting mix or a special growing mat. The steps are always the same: scatter the small seeds thickly and dry (no soaking needed), cover the tray to keep it dark for about 3 to 4 days while they sprout, then move it into the light to green up, then snip and eat. The taste is mild, fresh, and a little cabbage-like. Broccoli is one of the most popular microgreens because it is so nutritious, packed with the healthy plant compounds the cabbage family is known for, and young microgreens tend to be richer in vitamins than full-grown plants. There is no outdoor season or weather to worry about, so they grow the same way no matter where you live.
seasoned: Broccoli microgreens are the young seedlings of broccoli (Brassica oleracea var. italica), harvested at the cotyledon to first-true-leaf stage about 8 to 12 days after sowing. They are grown indoors year-round in a short repeatable cycle: a dense, dry, even sow on a shallow tray of mix or a fiber mat (broccoli needs no presoak), a brief dark blackout of about 3 to 4 days to drive even germination and stem stretch, then light to green up, then a single cut. The flavor is mild, fresh, and faintly cabbage-like. Broccoli is one of the most popular microgreens for nutrition; like other brassica microgreens it concentrates the glucosinolates that give the cabbage family its character, and research finds microgreens generally higher in vitamins and phytochemicals than the mature vegetable. Because there is no frost, season, or hardiness zone involved, the same tray grows identically on a windowsill anywhere.

beginner: Your broccoli microgreens are ready when the first little seed-leaves are open and, for many, the first true leaf is just showing, usually about 8 to 12 days after sowing and a couple of inches tall. Snip them just above the medium with clean scissors and eat them fresh. They do not grow back, so you start a new tray each time.
seasoned: Cut at the cotyledon to first-true-leaf stage, typically 8 to 12 days from sowing, when the stand is about 2 to 3 inches tall. Snip just above the medium with clean scissors; broccoli will not regrow, so the tray is a single cut.
